reviews.text: ...a typically verbose endeavor that grows more and more involving as it progresses...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Chasing Amy is just like my kid brother -- alternately adorable and exasperating and full of cocky witticisms about life with very little experience to back them up.
reviews.author: Cathay Che

reviews.text: With some wonderful jabs at gender and racial stereotypes, Chasing Amy eschews political correctness to explore sexual identity with more thoughtfulness than we’ve seen before, at least from a filmmaker who happens to be a 26-year-old straight guy.
reviews.author: Mark J. Huisman

reviews.text: What's best about Chasing Amy is that it matters in a way Smith's other films don't -- it throbs with real feelings and frustrated inadequacy.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: A reductive juncture in Smith's career compared to his more situationally-specific and fine-tuned predecessors, Clerks and Mallrats.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: With their matching hipster goatees and deadpan cynicism, Affleck and Lee evince the easy rapport of old buds.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: Slowly, like a latent teen pulled against his will into adulthood, Kevin Smith is growing up. But he's not growing quietly.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: There is a lot of frank conversation about the technical aspects of sex between women, but Holden and Banky are written more like sniggering eighth graders than inquisitive adults.
reviews.author: Paul Tatara

reviews.text: Chasing Amy represents a change in direction for Smith, with drama before gags. A chick flick for blokes.
The movie reinforces his gift for dialogue, but his ability to handle actors, compose scenes or keep track of his own story is negligible.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Chasing Amy often is convulsively funny.
reviews.author: Roger Hurlburt

reviews.text: [A] cool, hilarious and sexy romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: As in Smith's debut film, Clerks, there's something about the scruffy Chasing Amy that breaks through the pretenses of more conventional movies.
reviews.author: Jay Boyar

reviews.text: Even when its young, uncertain characters appear to be in danger of talking (and whining) themselves to death, there's something genuine and charmingly naive about their attempts to make sense of their feelings.
reviews.author: John Hartl

reviews.text: Although [Smith's] dialogue is often witty, he still relies on blunt sexual humor to get his point across.
reviews.author: David Sterritt

reviews.text: Affleck and Lee have a great comic thing going on.
reviews.author: Stephen Hunter

reviews.text: Chasing Amy is not yet a mature work Smith still needs a style to go with his sensibility but its yearning for maturity is palpable and touching.
reviews.author: Dave Kehr

reviews.text: The performances are universally strong. The goateed Affleck makes for a particularly sympathetic protagonist; he has the looks and confidence of a lady-killer, but nagging befuddlement and vulnerability are rarely far from the surface.
reviews.author: Mark Caro

reviews.text: Dated romantic comedy wrong for all kids.
reviews.author: Carly Kocurek

reviews.text: The third installment of Kevin Smith's New Jersey Trilogy is also the only Kevin Smith movie that's worth any serious attention.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Like a raw nerve tweaked over and over again by emotions both radiant and revealing, Chasing Amy is as close to a masterpiece as Smith has ever created.
reviews.author: Bill Gibron

reviews.text: Chasing Amy suggests that Smith could do so much better if only he would push himself.
reviews.author: Matt Noller

reviews.text: Smith's most mature film. Yes, it's filled with crude dialogue, blunt descriptions of sex and an overkill of Star Wars references, but it uses these to dig deeper and make its subject matter more accessible.
reviews.author: Ryan Cracknell

reviews.text: Smith isn't just fooling around anymore.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Neither PC nor crudely anti-PC, this tough and tender movie, like its characters, is prepared to take emotional risks, and the comic book milieu is deftly sketched in.
reviews.author: Jonathan Rosenbaum

reviews.text: Amusing and appealing.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Instead of cool twenty-something irony, Smith startles us with raw emotional honesty.
reviews.author: David Ansen

reviews.text: The plot and dialogue play too much as if Smith is re-enacting past romantic squabbles he's had, and rewriting them, too.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The script moves beyond Smith's customary cataloguing of male adolescent ignorance and idiocy to offer sharp insights into the romanticism and pragmatism, pride and double standards that define the tangled threesome.
reviews.author: Geoff Andrew

reviews.text: Like Clerks, this is a politically incorrect comedy with casual profanity, but more profoundly so. Smith doesn't play the Hollywood stereotype of lesbians as women who have not met yet the right guy.
reviews.author: Emanuel Levy

reviews.text: An intelligent and provocative low-budget film with big-budget talent and look, making it an exceptional independent effort.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: ...Smith makes raw and naturalistic, highly verbal films full of frank talk about sex; making the audience uncomfortable is part of the point.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: ... an important movie about young people lost in the Gen-X labyrinth who are giving it a try [and] risking their hearts to find some kind of answer.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: It is evident that Kevin Smith is maturing both as a writer and a human being.
reviews.author: Jeanne Aufmuth

reviews.text: Smith's handling of actors has improved considerably. Now if he would stop looking for some goofy hook to build his movies around.
reviews.author: Ron Wells

reviews.text: Indie god Kevin Smith's finest hour gets the Criterion treatment.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: Smith is at his best when he's letting his movie be silly. The more he chases significance, the more Chasing Amy fails to find its way.
reviews.author: Jeff Strickler

reviews.text: It's a tribute to a smartly written script that the triangular relationships are played out in hip, flip language, but are not trivialized. These characters may be wry, rude and foul-mouthed, but they are grappling with honest human emotion.
reviews.author: Margaret A. McGurk

reviews.text: No  difcil perceber quando um filme foi feito com carinho. 'Procura-se Amy'  um exemplo claro disso.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: It takes guts to make a personal film, and Smith's tender characterization of Alyssa proves he's got the goods. Never mind the convenience store or the mall: this time he dares to set his New Jersey story in the heart.
reviews.author: Alicia Potter

reviews.text: Covers the tricky turf of sexual politics with zest and creativity.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Can a script exploring some truly deep questions about human sexuality and emotions be any shoddier and wooden? Will Miramax continue to fund one of the worst directors in the business? Don't stay tuned.
reviews.author: Eric Brace

reviews.text: Smith has apprehended something profound about the fluidity of sexual identity and the solipsism that drives a wedge between even the most passionate lovers.
reviews.author: Stephen Farber

reviews.text: It's fun and infantile and vulgar, like Clerks, but with a really mature message and well-developed characters.
reviews.author: Karina Montgomery

reviews.text: Utilises the same sharp - sometimes sick - observational humour and ear for dialogue that made Clerks such an indie gem.
reviews.author: Jane Crowther

reviews.text: tackles issues and explores situations that many other filmmakers have shied away from
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: ...rivals a 1930s screwball comedy -- although the subject matter certainly does not.
reviews.author: Rob Blackwelder

reviews.text: It's a rude blast of gleeful provocation, a farce about emotional pain, a drama about sexual slapstick.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Work of such fierce intelligence and emotional honesty that it blows away the competition when it comes to contemporary romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Kevin Thomas

reviews.text: Well-acted and directed and proves to be a very moving and personal film.
reviews.author: Mark R. Leeper

reviews.text: The jealousy, confusion, and wounded emotions that come into play here are tightly woven and deftly handled.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: A well-written and acted romantic drama that marks a step forward in the promising career of Kevin Smith.
reviews.author: Dan Jardine

reviews.text: As Chasing Amy redefines the boy-meets-girl formula for a culture where anything goes, including perhaps another boy or girl, it thrives on Smith's dry, deadpan direction.
reviews.author: Janet Maslin

reviews.text: Smith gives Chasing Amy both a wicked sense of humor and a genuine sensitivity about the complications of sexual politics.
reviews.author: Scott Renshaw

reviews.text: For all its false steps and the occasional dubious philosophical stance, it's an exhilarating movie.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: While this dark, perceptive variation on the romantic comedy genre doesn't quite match the former's [Clerks] majesty, it still marks a triumphant return to form.
reviews.author: Caroline Westbrook

reviews.text: Smith's most provocative outing yet and certainly the toughest to forget.
reviews.author: Mike Clark

reviews.text: A brutally honest romance. If you loved Sleepless in Seattle, you'll just hate it.
reviews.author: Richard Schickel

reviews.text: In-your-face with an attitude that's as tactless as it is honest.
reviews.author: Joe Baltake

reviews.text: It's too loud, sometimes, and it's always pushy, but it's got heart.
reviews.author: Mary Brennan

reviews.text: Many of the situations in the film, sexual and otherwise, seem forced and don't ring true.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: Smith makes it crackle, with various aggressive honesties and wit.
reviews.author: Stanley Kauffmann

reviews.text: What Smith does best in Chasing Amy is write clever, raunchy and emotionally true-to-life dialogue, particularly in the arguments between Holden and Alyssa.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: It is surprisingly warm, charming and even thoughful at times, although the ending feels forced and the whole thing seems at least 10 minutes too long.
reviews.author: Jeff Vice

reviews.text: The story is a refreshing twist on the standard romantic comedy, but something about Kevin Smith's style leaves me feeling a little dirty.
reviews.author: Marty Mapes

reviews.text: Many films try to explore the romantic and sexual dynamics between men and women. Few do it as provocatively, humorously, or bravely as Chasing Amy.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The film gets more mileage out of its setup than I thought possible.
reviews.author: Steve Rhodes

reviews.text: Funny, fearless... and profoundly moving. Never did I ever think I'd come away from a Smith film with a lump in my throat.
reviews.author: Michael Dequina

reviews.text: As funny as the observational outrage humor of Clerks, but Smith is working harder.
reviews.author: Jeff Millar

reviews.text: Although the intermittent stupidity and vulgarity of Smith's characters is sometimes painful to watch, the film's refreshing realism is an invaluable experience.
reviews.author: Bradley Null

reviews.text: Sharp, insightful, highly personal dramedy about relationships between lovers and friends.
reviews.author: Betsy Bozdech

reviews.text: There's a decent plot and substantial characters in the mix as well. There are a few times when the plot begins to meander as it wallows in its trivialities, but soon it is back up and kicking.
reviews.author: Madeleine Williams

reviews.text: Hip, clever, and outrageous
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: Often funny but ultimately wrenching
reviews.author: Susan Stark

reviews.text: Funny, romantic, and a bit challenging.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: One of the most impressive aspects of Chasing Amy is that its alleged hero is often wildly unsympathetic, and intentionally so.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: The premise is unusual, the impact is overwhelming.
reviews.author: Urban Cinefile Critics

reviews.text: Make Holden and Banky and Alyssa ten years older -- in other words, make them Boomers -- and you've got Seinfeld.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: This movie is about something, and the deeper we get into it, the more we realize how emotionally on-target the script is.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: While the surface of his film sparkles with sharp, ironic dialogue, deeper issues are forming, and Chasing Amy develops into a film of touching insights.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: Kevin Smith seems to be spilling his guts in this movie.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: Lacks insight and finesse, and feels like a boldfaced Rorschach for Smith's own hang-ups.
reviews.author: Edward Guthmann

reviews.text: Though flawed, the Generation-X romantic comedy offers appealing characters and quite a few legitimate laughs.
reviews.author: Jack Garner

reviews.text: It could prove to be as bad a date movie for some couples as it might be a real turn-on for others. Anyone with set ideas about sex roles or orientations is likely to get steamed.
reviews.author: Charles Taylor

reviews.text: Not everything worked or made sense, but the characters and their problems seemed real.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

synopsis: Holden and Banky are best friends and authors of a popular comic book. Holden falls in love with Alyssa, who happens to be a lesbian. Holden's relationship with Alyssa strains his life-long friendship with Banky, and soon the relationship between Holden and Alyssa has problems when he cannot deal with her past.
